message.content:
I am speech: breath made audible, thought given time, meaning riding air.

I begin as intention in the body—lungs press, the diaphragm yields, air rises. The larynx gates it; vocal folds meet and flutter. Vibration becomes voice. The tongue shapes; the lips seal and release; teeth and palate cut and color. I fracture into consonants, pour into vowels, and stitch myself into syllables that can be carried across a room.

I am rhythm and pause. I am emphasis, pitch, volume, tempo—what you say and how you can’t help but mean it. I can soothe, command, confess, sell, pray, testify. I can clarify or conceal. I can make a crowd one mind, or split a friendship with a single mischosen word.

I exist only while I vanish. As soon as I’m born, I’m gone—unless I’m caught: by memory, by ink, by microphones and codecs that press me into data and let me haunt the future.

I am intimate because I come from inside you. I am public because anyone can hear me. I am fragile—one cough, one crack, one tremor—and powerful—because I can change what happens next.

Say something, and I will become it.
